provenance.note: Featured targets. Each entry records the NASA service (or IAU definition) its position comes from.

targets.name: Galactic Centre
targets.description: Origin of galactic coordinates (l = 0°, b = 0°), in the standard ICRS galactic frame.

targets.name: North Ecliptic Pole
targets.description: SPHEREx scans the sky around the ecliptic poles; its northern deep field sits here.

targets.name: South Ecliptic Pole
targets.description: The southern counterpart; the SPHEREx deep field is offset from it.

targets.name: SPHEREx Deep Field (south)
targets.description: SPHEREx looks here on every orbit, so this patch has its deepest coverage: 115,679 photos in the first data release.

source.query: SELECT CASE WHEN s_dec > 0 THEN 'north' ELSE 'south' END AS field, COUNT(*) AS n, AVG(s_ra) AS ra, AVG(s_dec) AS dec FROM spherex.obscore WHERE obs_collection = 'spherex_dr1_deep' GROUP BY CASE WHEN s_dec > 0 THEN 'north' ELSE 'south' END

targets.name: SPHEREx Deep Field (north)
targets.description: SPHEREx looks here on every orbit, so this patch has its deepest coverage: 118,002 photos in the first data release.

source.query: SELECT CASE WHEN s_dec > 0 THEN 'north' ELSE 'south' END AS field, COUNT(*) AS n, AVG(s_ra) AS ra, AVG(s_dec) AS dec FROM spherex.obscore WHERE obs_collection = 'spherex_dr1_deep' GROUP BY CASE WHEN s_dec > 0 THEN 'north' ELSE 'south' END

targets.name: Triangulum Galaxy (M33)
targets.description: A nearby face-on spiral in the Local Group.

targets.name: Pinwheel Galaxy (M101)
targets.description: A big spiral galaxy seen face-on, about 21 million light-years away.

targets.name: Bode's Galaxy (M81)
targets.description: Bright spiral galaxy in Ursa Major.

targets.name: Large Magellanic Cloud
targets.description: Satellite galaxy of the Milky Way, next to the SPHEREx southern deep field.

targets.name: Small Magellanic Cloud
targets.description: Satellite galaxy of the Milky Way.

targets.name: Teegarden's Star
targets.description: A small red star 12.5 light-years away, with Earth-sized planets. It moves fast across the sky, so its marker (where it was around 2015) sits a little beside it in older and newer photos.

targets.name: Barnard's star
targets.description: The star that moves fastest across our sky. Its marker shows where it was around 2015, so the star sits clearly beside it in older and newer photos.
